replay_method: Re-derive K_k future behavior from the static graph, fixed seed and exact palette semantics. Treat the primary carrier theorem as the object under test, not an assumption.

current_profile_palettes: Every live l_i sees fixed s4=4 and no forced L neighbor, so A(l_i)={1,2,3}.
Let m=max(F), m=0 for F empty. r_j sees forced color 1 iff j<=m, hence A(r_j)={2,3} for j<=m and {1,2,3} otherwise.
R1: If u=l_i, every c in {1,2,3} is extendable by choosing a different uniform color on R.
If u=r_j and c=2 or 3, color all live L by a different color and all R by c.
If u=r_j and c=1, palette admissibility implies j>m, so no forced l_h is adjacent to r_j. Set r_j=1, all other R=2 and all live L=3.
Thus R1(u,c)=1 exactly for c in A(u).
R2_same_side: For two live L vertices, assign both the query color and color R uniformly with a different color chosen to avoid fixed L=1 where necessary.

For two live R vertices, colors 2/3 extend by a uniform opposite-side color; color 1 is palette-admissible only when both indices exceed m, and then no forced L is adjacent to either target. Set targets 1, other R 2 and live L 3.
Hence every same-side nonedge query with c in both palettes is extendable.
R2_cross_nonedge: A cross nonedge is l_i-r_j with j>i.
For c=1, palette admissibility at r_j gives j>m. Set r_j and all live l_h with h<j to 1, all live l_h with h>=j to 3, and all other R to 2.
For c=2, use color 2 below threshold j and color 1 at/above j on L, with all other R=3.
For c=3, use color 3 below threshold j and color 1 at/above j on L, with all other R=2.
Every chain edge has differently colored endpoints. Thus R2 equals nonedge plus palette intersection.
behavior_collapse: On coordinates live in two D-profiles with the same m, the R1/R2 truth tables coincide.
If m<m', then R1(r_j,1) for any m<j<=m' separates the profiles.
Different forced subsets with the same m may remain distinct only through live-domain/reconstruction identity information, which is encoded by an O(k)-bit vector.
carrier: Every L/R vertex is adjacent to fixed s4=4, so color 4 is globally unavailable on the entire chain core for every future state.
If z is unfixed, assigning z=4 is always legal relative to R because R can never use 4.
If z is fixed to 1,2 or 3, its color is merely deleted from every active R list.
After any fixed assignments, each remaining active L/R list is therefore a subset of common palette {1,2,3}.
The active L/R graph is an induced subgraph of the original chain graph and hence P7-free.
Constructive P7-free List-3 exactly decides the remaining extension problem and returns a witness.
update_reconstruction: A legal future R1/R2 update changes only O(1) fixed-status entries before the sealed B2B1 canonicalizer runs.
Any canonical deletion is stored by an independent receipt; deleted vertices cannot be future query targets.
The carrier stores ACTIVE/FIXED/DELETED plus fixed color/receipt pointer per original vertex, so its description is O(k).
Reconstruction concatenates fixed assignments, the List-3 witness, z=4 when unfixed, and deleted-component receipts.
